transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’m just not sleeping in any way that feels useful anymore. I lie there awake, going over client models in my head, and then I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach tight. By the time I go to work, it feels like I never actually rested.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things in your life, even when there isn't an immediate problem?
I’m not sure I’d call it excessive. I do think things over a lot, especially when I’m trying to settle down, but I don’t always know if that’s worry or just… my mind not shutting off.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying thoughts once they start, even when you try to distract yourself or relax?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid attention to whether I can stop it, exactly. Sometimes I try to distract myself, but I can’t always tell if it’s worry or just my mind staying busy. I don’t have a clear answer.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, muscle tension, or being easily fatigued, even when you're not actively thinking about anything?
I don’t really know. I haven’t paid close attention to whether I feel tense or on edge when I’m not thinking about something. I do feel worn down a lot, but I’m not sure what to connect that to.
Do you find yourself worrying about a variety of things in your life, like work, relationships, or health, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear sense that I’m worrying about all those areas, like work and health and relationships, when nothing is going on. I may think about things, but I can’t say it feels like constant worry about a variety of things.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because your mind is racing or you feel anxious, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?

Yes. That’s honestly a big part of why I came in. I barely sleep in a way that feels useful anymore. I’ll lie there replaying client models in my head, and then I’m up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach tight. Then I go to work feeling like I never really rested.
Do you often feel tired or low on energy even when you haven’t had trouble sleeping, or does this fatigue only happen after a poor night’s sleep?

It’s mostly tied to the sleep, I think. I came in because I barely sleep in any way that feels useful anymore. I lie there replaying client models, then I’m awake again at 3 or 4 with my stomach tight, and by the time I get to work I feel like I never actually rested.
Have you found yourself feeling down, depressed, or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, even when your sleep is okay?

Yes. Even when sleep isn’t the main issue, most days I just feel… down. I move through work and then go home to my apartment with this heavy, gray feeling, like I’m just going through the motions. Sometimes someone asks me a normal question and I have to try not to cry.
Have you lost interest or found less pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, even when you’re not feeling tired or down?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I know I don’t do much for enjoyment lately, but it’s hard for me to separate whether I’ve lost interest from just being tired or feeling low. I haven’t really noticed it as its own thing.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate or focus, like difficulty paying attention at work or finishing tasks because your mind feels foggy or distracted?

Yes. That’s been a real problem at work. Spreadsheets and models that used to feel automatic now take me hours, because I lose track of what I was doing. I’ll reread the same assumptions over and over and still feel unsure, like I must have missed something obvious before a presentation.
Have you noticed any days where you feel down or lose interest in things even when you’ve had a decent night’s sleep?

Yes. Even if I sleep okay, I still have a lot of days where I feel heavy and gray. I’ll get through the office, come home, and it just feels like I’m going through the motions. Sometimes even a simple question from someone makes me feel like I might cry.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight, like eating more or less than usual, even when your sleep has been okay?

I haven’t really noticed a clear change there. My appetite kind of varies day to day, but I can’t say I’ve been eating much more or much less than usual, and I haven’t been tracking my weight closely.
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or guilty about things, even when there doesn’t seem to be a clear reason for it?

Yes. Especially at work. If my manager questions one of my projections, I immediately take it as proof that I’m not as sharp as I used to be. It’s like I assume everyone can see I’m failing, even if it’s just a normal question.
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying, or found yourself wishing you weren’t awake, even just fleetingly?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I really don’t want to deal with the day, but I can’t say I’ve been thinking about death or wishing I wouldn’t wake up.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still, even when you're not trying to sleep or focus on something?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself moving especially slowly, and I don’t think I’ve been pacing or unable to sit still in a way that stands out. If it’s happening, it’s not something I’ve clearly picked up on.

Have you noticed yourself feeling slowed down or moving more slowly than usual, or on the opposite end, feeling restless and unable to sit still, even when you're not trying to sleep or focus on something?

I think I’d answer the same way—I haven’t really noticed that. I don’t feel like I’m moving unusually slowly, and I’m not pacing around or unable to sit still. Nothing that stands out to me, at least.
Do you find yourself worrying about a number of different things in your life, such as work, relationships, health, or other responsibilities, even when there isn't an immediate problem?

I’m not sure. I mean, I do think about responsibilities and things I have to handle, but I don’t know that I’d call it worrying about lots of different things when there isn’t a problem. Nothing specific really comes to mind.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the heaviness and loss of interest most days?
It’s been about three years now. It really started after the merger, when they reorganized our Caribbean-market division, and it’s just kind of stayed with me most days since then.
Have there been times when you felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks or more in a row, even if you were sleeping okay during that time?

Yes. It’s been more than two weeks at a time, definitely. Most days I’m at the office or even just at home, and there’s this heavy, gray feeling. I feel like I’m just going through the motions, and sometimes if someone asks me a normal question, I’m trying not to cry.
